description.narrative:
Stakeholder Effects: Improved access to finance for MSEs, including WMSEs: The project will help to address the MSME finance gap in Uzbekistan which in 2019 was estimated to be over US$11 billion or approximately 18% of the countrys GDP, by providing much needed financing for MSEs and grow its financing to WMSEs and to assist them in overcoming liquidity constraints.
Inclusiveness: IFC anticipates that the project will promote the inclusiveness of the Uzbek financial markets by showcasing a rigorous increase of the Banks engagement with the women segment. Currently, the Uzbek financial sector offers a few specialized loans for women, yet no other financial products for women such as deposits and savings, insurance, or payments and money transfers, or women-specific service bundles.

The proposed investment in the existing IFC portfolio client, Private Joint Stock Commercial Bank Davr Bank (Davr or the Bank), consists of a senior loan package of up to US$60 million. This package includes: (i) an A loan of up to US$30 million, to be committed in two tranches: (a) a US$20 million USD loan; and (b) a US$10 million UZS-linked loan; and (ii) B1 Loan/Parallel Loan of up to US$30 million. The loan proceeds will be used for financing micro and small enterprises (MSEs), with at least 80% of total proceeds allocated to MSEs and no less than 40% of total proceeds on-lent to Women-Owned Business (WMSEs).
